title: HTML5 Foundations

lessons.title: 1. What is HTML?
lessons.explanationHtml:
📌 What is it?

  • HTML (HyperText Markup Language) builds the skeleton of every website.

💡 Daily Life Example

  • Like the wooden or steel frame of a house before adding bricks or paint.

🎯 Real-World Usage

  • Creating headings, text, images, and buttons on web pages.

⚠️ Common Mistake

  • ❌ Confusing HTML with a programming language. It is a markup language!

📝 Quick Task

  • Create your first .html file in VS Code.
lessons.codeExample:
/* What is HTML? Example */
console.log("What is HTML?");

lessons.explanationHtml:

lessons.explanationHtml:

  • Controls font-family, font-size, font-weight, and line-height.

lessons.title: 6. The Box Model (Padding & Margin)
lessons.explanationHtml:
📌 What is it?

  • Every element is a box with Content, Padding, Border, and Margin.

💡 Daily Life Example

  • Padding = Bubble wrap inside a package; Margin = Space between two packages on a shelf.

  • Spacing out text and buttons on a web page.

⚠️ Common Mistake

lessons.explanationHtml:

  • Preventing layout overflow bugs globally.

  • ❌ Forgetting to set * { box-sizing: border-box; } globally.

title: React Fundamentals
description: Master React step-by-step with simple English, daily life examples, and bullet points across 25 lessons.

lessons.title: 1. What is React?
lessons.explanationHtml:
📌 What is it?

  • React is a JavaScript library for building component-based user interfaces.

💡 Daily Life Example

  • Building a castle using reusable LEGO bricks instead of carving one giant rock.

🎯 Real-World Usage

  • Powering Facebook, Netflix, Airbnb, and Instagram.

⚠️ Common Mistake

  • ❌ Thinking React is a full framework (It is a UI library!).

📝 Quick Task

  • Create your first React component using Vite.
lessons.codeExample:
// What is React? Example
console.log("What is React?");

lessons.title: 2. JSX (JavaScript XML)
lessons.explanationHtml:
📌 What is it?

  • JSX allows you to write HTML-like tags directly inside JavaScript files.

💡 Daily Life Example

  • Mixing fruit slices directly into yogurt to make a fruit parfait.

🎯 Real-World Usage

  • Defining component structures with embedded dynamic variables.

⚠️ Common Mistake

  • ❌ Using class instead of className attribute in JSX.

📝 Quick Task

  • Render a

    with dynamic variable {name} in JSX.
lessons.codeExample:
// JSX (JavaScript XML) Example
console.log("JSX (JavaScript XML)");

lessons.title: 3. Components (Functional)
lessons.explanationHtml:
📌 What is it?

  • Components are reusable functions returning JSX UI elements.

💡 Daily Life Example

  • Stamping out cookies using a custom cookie cutter.

🎯 Real-World Usage

  • Building Navbars, Product Cards, and Buttons.

⚠️ Common Mistake

  • ❌ Component names MUST start with a Capital letter (e.g. Card, not card).

📝 Quick Task

  • Create a functional component named WelcomeMessage.
lessons.codeExample:
// Components (Functional) Example
console.log("Components (Functional)");

lessons.title: 4. Props (Passing Data)
lessons.explanationHtml:
📌 What is it?

  • Props pass data down from parent component to child component.

💡 Daily Life Example

  • Passing a wrapped gift box to your friend.

🎯 Real-World Usage

  • Customizing buttons, user profiles, and cards with dynamic data.

⚠️ Common Mistake

  • ❌ Trying to mutate/modify props inside child component (Props are read-only!).

📝 Quick Task

  • Pass a title prop to a Header component.
lessons.codeExample:
// Props (Passing Data) Example
console.log("Props (Passing Data)");

lessons.title: 5. State (useState Hook)
lessons.explanationHtml:
📌 What is it?

  • State holds dynamic component memory that triggers re-renders when updated.

💡 Daily Life Example

  • A digital scoreboard updating when a team scores a goal.

🎯 Real-World Usage

  • Form inputs, shopping cart counts, and toggle switches.

⚠️ Common Mistake

  • ❌ Mutating state directly e.g. state = 5 instead of setState(5).

📝 Quick Task

  • Create a counter component using useState.
lessons.codeExample:
// State (useState Hook) Example
console.log("State (useState Hook)");

lessons.title: 6. Handling Events
lessons.explanationHtml:
📌 What is it?

  • Attaches event handlers like onClick={() => handleClick()}.

💡 Daily Life Example

  • Pressing the electric horn button on a bicycle handlebar.

🎯 Real-World Usage

  • Handling button clicks and form submits in React.

⚠️ Common Mistake

  • ❌ Calling function immediately: onClick={handleClick()} instead of onClick={handleClick}.

📝 Quick Task

  • Add an onClick handler to a button that alerts a message.
lessons.codeExample:
// Handling Events Example
console.log("Handling Events");

lessons.title: 7. Conditional Rendering
lessons.explanationHtml:
📌 What is it?

  • Displays different UI elements based on boolean conditions using && or ternary ? :.

💡 Daily Life Example

  • A sign showing 'OPEN' when store is open, or 'CLOSED' when shut.

🎯 Real-World Usage

  • Showing loading spinners, login buttons, or error banners.

⚠️ Common Mistake

  • ❌ Returning undefined or null accidentally.

📝 Quick Task

  • Render a message if isLoggedIn is true.
lessons.codeExample:
// Conditional Rendering Example
console.log("Conditional Rendering");

lessons.title: 8. Rendering Lists & Keys
lessons.explanationHtml:
📌 What is it?

  • Renders array lists using .map() with unique key props.

💡 Daily Life Example

  • Assigning coat check tags (keys) to every coat in a closet.

🎯 Real-World Usage

  • Displaying product catalogs and comment sections.

⚠️ Common Mistake

  • ❌ Forgetting key prop on list items, causing re-render performance issues.

📝 Quick Task

  • Map over an array of items and render
  • tags with unique keys.
lessons.codeExample:
// Rendering Lists & Keys Example
console.log("Rendering Lists & Keys");

lessons.title: 9. Form Handling in React
lessons.explanationHtml:
📌 What is it?

  • Binds form inputs to React state (Controlled Components).

💡 Daily Life Example

  • Steering a car where your hands on the wheel (state) dictate direction.

🎯 Real-World Usage

  • Login forms, search filters, and checkout fields.

⚠️ Common Mistake

  • ❌ Forgetting e.preventDefault() on form submit.

📝 Quick Task

  • Create a controlled text input storing value in useState.
lessons.codeExample:
// Form Handling in React Example
console.log("Form Handling in React");

lessons.title: 10. Effects (useEffect Hook)
lessons.explanationHtml:
📌 What is it?

  • Runs side effects like data fetching, subscriptions, or DOM updates.

💡 Daily Life Example

  • An alarm clock ringing when a timer reaches zero.

🎯 Real-World Usage

  • Fetching API data on component mount.

⚠️ Common Mistake

  • ❌ Forgetting dependency array [], causing infinite fetch loops!

📝 Quick Task

  • Add useEffect running once on mount with [] dependency array.
lessons.codeExample:
// Effects (useEffect Hook) Example
console.log("Effects (useEffect Hook)");

lessons.title: 11. Data Fetching with useEffect
lessons.explanationHtml:
📌 What is it?

  • Fetches live data inside useEffect and saves it into useState.

💡 Daily Life Example

  • A waiter fetching your dish from the kitchen and bringing it to your table.

🎯 Real-World Usage

  • Loading user profile, posts, and notifications.

⚠️ Common Mistake

  • ❌ Not handling loading or error states during fetch.

📝 Quick Task

  • Fetch sample JSON data inside useEffect.
lessons.codeExample:
// Data Fetching with useEffect Example
console.log("Data Fetching with useEffect");

lessons.title: 12. Custom Hooks
lessons.explanationHtml:
📌 What is it?

  • Extracts reusable stateful logic into custom use... functions.

💡 Daily Life Example

  • Packaging a custom universal charging cable for all your devices.

🎯 Real-World Usage

  • useFetch, useLocalStorage, useWindowSize.

⚠️ Common Mistake

  • ❌ Custom hook names MUST start with 'use' prefix.

📝 Quick Task

  • Create a custom hook useCounter.
lessons.codeExample:
// Custom Hooks Example
console.log("Custom Hooks");

lessons.title: 13. Component Lifecycle
lessons.explanationHtml:
📌 What is it?

  • Mounting (birth), Updating (life), and Unmounting (death) stages.

💡 Daily Life Example

  • Planting a seed, watering it as it grows, and clearing it when withered.

🎯 Real-World Usage

  • Cleaning up timers and event listeners when components unmount.

⚠️ Common Mistake

  • ❌ Memory leaks caused by not clearing setInterval on unmount.

📝 Quick Task

  • Return a cleanup function from useEffect to clear an interval.
lessons.codeExample:
// Component Lifecycle Example
console.log("Component Lifecycle");

lessons.title: 14. Refs (useRef Hook)
lessons.explanationHtml:
📌 What is it?

  • Persists mutable values across renders without triggering a re-render.

💡 Daily Life Example

  • Writing a secret note on a paper in your pocket.

🎯 Real-World Usage

  • Focusing text inputs manually or measuring DOM elements.

⚠️ Common Mistake

  • ❌ Overusing useRef for state that should trigger UI updates.

📝 Quick Task

  • Focus an input field using useRef when a button is clicked.
lessons.codeExample:
// Refs (useRef Hook) Example
console.log("Refs (useRef Hook)");

lessons.title: 15. Context API (Global State)
lessons.explanationHtml:
📌 What is it?

  • Shares state across entire component tree without prop drilling.

💡 Daily Life Example

  • A radio broadcast station sending audio to all cars in the city simultaneously.

🎯 Real-World Usage

  • User authentication state, dark mode theme, and shopping cart.

⚠️ Common Mistake

  • ❌ Wrapping everything in Context, causing unnecessary re-renders.

📝 Quick Task

  • Create a ThemeContext providing 'dark' or 'light' theme.
lessons.codeExample:
// Context API (Global State) Example
console.log("Context API (Global State)");

lessons.title: 16. useReducer Hook
lessons.explanationHtml:
📌 What is it?

  • Manages complex state logic via dispatching actions to a reducer function.

💡 Daily Life Example

  • A bank manager processing deposit/withdraw slips at a desk counter.

🎯 Real-World Usage

  • Complex forms and multi-step cart checkouts.

⚠️ Common Mistake

  • ❌ Mutating state directly inside reducer instead of returning new state.

📝 Quick Task

  • Write a simple reducer handling 'INCREMENT' and 'DECREMENT' actions.
lessons.codeExample:
// useReducer Hook Example

lessons.title: 17. React Router (Client Navigation)
lessons.explanationHtml:
📌 What is it?

  • Navigates between pages without full browser page reloads.

💡 Daily Life Example

  • Switching channels on your TV instant screen refresh.

🎯 Real-World Usage

  • Single Page Application (SPA) routing.

⚠️ Common Mistake

  • ❌ Using tags instead of component from react-router-dom.

📝 Quick Task

  • Add a button.

lessons.title: 18. Performance Memoization (useMemo)
lessons.explanationHtml:
📌 What is it?

  • Caches expensive calculation results between renders.

💡 Daily Life Example

  • Writing down the answer to a hard math problem on a sticky note to re-read later.

🎯 Real-World Usage

  • Filtering 10,000 table rows efficiently.

⚠️ Common Mistake

  • ❌ Over-optimizing cheap inline math operations with useMemo.

📝 Quick Task

  • Memoize a list sorting calculation.
lessons.codeExample:

lessons.title: 19. useCallback Hook
lessons.explanationHtml:
📌 What is it?

  • Caches function definitions between re-renders.

💡 Daily Life Example

  • Saving a speed-dial contact on your phone.

🎯 Real-World Usage

  • Preventing child component re-renders when passing callbacks.

⚠️ Common Mistake

  • ❌ Forgetting dependency array in useCallback.

    elements.

  • Scopes CSS classes locally to prevent class name collisions.

  • Assigning private house numbers on private streets.

🎯 Real-World Usage

  • Component-level isolated styling.

lessons.explanationHtml:

title: SQL Fundamentals
description: Master SQL databases step-by-step with simple English, daily life examples, and bullet points across 25 lessons.

lessons.title: 1. What is SQL?
lessons.explanationHtml:
📌 What is it?

  • SQL (Structured Query Language) is the language used to communicate with Relational Databases.

💡 Daily Life Example

  • Asking a librarian to find a specific book in a organized library.

🎯 Real-World Usage

  • Managing data in PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, and SQL Server.

⚠️ Common Mistake

  • ❌ Thinking SQL is a database (SQL is the language; Postgres/SQLite is the database system!).

📝 Quick Task

  • Write SELECT 'Hello SQL!';
lessons.codeExample:
// What is SQL? Example
console.log("What is SQL?");

lessons.title: 2. Databases & Tables
lessons.explanationHtml:
📌 What is it?

  • Databases store tables; Tables organize data into Rows and Columns.

💡 Daily Life Example

  • Database = A filing cabinet; Table = A single spreadsheet folder inside.

🎯 Real-World Usage

  • Storing Users, Products, Orders, and Payments.

⚠️ Common Mistake

  • ❌ Storing unrelated data together in a single mega-table.

📝 Quick Task

  • Identify table names in a database schema.
lessons.codeExample:
// Databases & Tables Example
console.log("Databases & Tables");

lessons.title: 3. Creating Tables (CREATE TABLE)
lessons.explanationHtml:
📌 What is it?

  • Defines table structure, columns, and data types.

💡 Daily Life Example

  • Setting up column headers (Name, Age, Email) in a brand new Excel sheet.

🎯 Real-World Usage

  • Database schema design.

⚠️ Common Mistake

  • ❌ Forgetting data types for columns.

📝 Quick Task

  • Write a CREATE TABLE query for a Users table.
lessons.codeExample:
// Creating Tables (CREATE TABLE) Example
console.log("Creating Tables (CREATE TABLE)");

lessons.title: 4. Data Types in SQL
lessons.explanationHtml:
📌 What is it?

  • Defines what type of data each column holds (VARCHAR, INT, FLOAT, BOOLEAN, TIMESTAMP).

💡 Daily Life Example

  • Setting input rules: Phone number field only accepts digits.

🎯 Real-World Usage

  • Ensuring database data integrity.

⚠️ Common Mistake

  • ❌ Using VARCHAR string type for numbers used in math calculations.

📝 Quick Task

  • Choose appropriate data types for a Products table.
lessons.codeExample:
// Data Types in SQL Example
console.log("Data Types in SQL");

lessons.title: 5. Inserting Data (INSERT INTO)
lessons.explanationHtml:
📌 What is it?

  • Adds new rows of data into a table.

💡 Daily Life Example

  • Filing a new paper form into a drawer folder.

🎯 Real-World Usage

  • User registration, creating new orders, adding blog posts.

⚠️ Common Mistake

  • ❌ Mismatching value count with column count in INSERT statement.

📝 Quick Task

  • Insert a new row into Users table.
lessons.codeExample:
// Inserting Data (INSERT INTO) Example
console.log("Inserting Data (INSERT INTO)");

lessons.title: 6. Selecting Data (SELECT)
lessons.explanationHtml:
📌 What is it?

  • Retrieves data columns from a table.

💡 Daily Life Example

  • Opening a folder and pulling out specific sheets of paper.

🎯 Real-World Usage

  • Displaying data on website dashboards.

⚠️ Common Mistake

  • ❌ Overusing SELECT * in production when you only need 2 columns.

📝 Quick Task

  • Select name and email from Users table.
lessons.codeExample:
// Selecting Data (SELECT) Example

lessons.title: 7. Filtering Data (WHERE Clause)
lessons.explanationHtml:
📌 What is it?

  • Filters query results based on conditions.

💡 Daily Life Example

  • Searching a contacts list for people living in 'Mumbai'.

🎯 Real-World Usage

  • Filtering products by price, searching users by email.

⚠️ Common Mistake

  • ❌ Forgetting quotes around string values in WHERE clause e.g. WHERE city = Mumbai.

📝 Quick Task

  • Select users WHERE age >= 18.
lessons.codeExample:
// Filtering Data (WHERE Clause) Example

lessons.title: 8. AND, OR, NOT Operators
lessons.explanationHtml:
📌 What is it?

  • Combines multiple search conditions in WHERE clause.

💡 Daily Life Example

  • Finding a car that is 'Red' AND 'Under $10,000'.

🎯 Real-World Usage

  • Complex catalog filtering on e-commerce sites.

⚠️ Common Mistake

  • ❌ Confusing AND (both true) with OR (either true).

📝 Quick Task

  • Select products WHERE price < 500 AND category = 'Electronics'.
lessons.codeExample:
// AND, OR, NOT Operators Example
console.log("AND, OR, NOT Operators");

lessons.title: 9. Updating Data (UPDATE)
lessons.explanationHtml:
📌 What is it?

  • Modifies existing records in a table.

💡 Daily Life Example

  • Using white-out to correct an address on an existing paper form.

🎯 Real-World Usage

  • Updating user profile, changing password, updating inventory count.

⚠️ Common Mistake

  • ⚠️ CRITICAL: Forgetting WHERE clause in UPDATE changes EVERY row in the database!

📝 Quick Task

  • Update user email WHERE id = 1.
lessons.codeExample:
// Updating Data (UPDATE) Example
console.log("Updating Data (UPDATE)");

lessons.title: 10. Deleting Data (DELETE FROM)
lessons.explanationHtml:
📌 What is it?

  • Removes specific rows from a table.

💡 Daily Life Example

  • Shredding an outdated document from your files.

🎯 Real-World Usage

  • Deleting cancelled accounts or old log entries.

⚠️ Common Mistake

  • ⚠️ CRITICAL: Forgetting WHERE clause in DELETE wipes the entire table!

📝 Quick Task

  • Delete user WHERE id = 5.
lessons.codeExample:
// Deleting Data (DELETE FROM) Example
console.log("Deleting Data (DELETE FROM)");

lessons.title: 11. Primary Keys (PRIMARY KEY)
lessons.explanationHtml:
📌 What is it?

  • Unique identifier column for every single row in a table.

💡 Daily Life Example

  • Your Aadhaar / Social Security / Passport ID number.

🎯 Real-World Usage

  • Uniquely identifying users, orders, and products.

⚠️ Common Mistake

  • ❌ Creating a table without a Primary Key.

📝 Quick Task

  • Define id INT PRIMARY KEY AUTO_INCREMENT in table creation.
lessons.codeExample:

lessons.title: 12. Sorting Results (ORDER BY)
lessons.explanationHtml:
📌 What is it?

  • Sorts query output in ASCending or DESCending order.

💡 Daily Life Example

  • Sorting exam papers alphabetically by student name or by highest score.

🎯 Real-World Usage

  • Displaying latest blog posts (ORDER BY created_at DESC).

⚠️ Common Mistake

  • ❌ Default sorting without specifying ASC or DESC.

📝 Quick Task

  • Select products ORDER BY price DESC.

lessons.title: 13. Limiting Results (LIMIT & OFFSET)
lessons.explanationHtml:
📌 What is it?

  • LIMIT caps number of rows returned; OFFSET skips rows.

💡 Daily Life Example

  • Reading page 2 of a book (10 lines per page).

🎯 Real-World Usage

  • Implementing website pagination (Page 1, Page 2).

⚠️ Common Mistake

  • ❌ Fetching 1,000,000 rows without a LIMIT.

📝 Quick Task

  • Select top 5 cheapest items using LIMIT 5.

lessons.title: 14. Aggregate Functions (COUNT, SUM, AVG)
lessons.explanationHtml:
📌 What is it?

  • Calculates total counts, sums, or averages across rows.

💡 Daily Life Example

  • Using a calculator to total up monthly grocery receipts.

🎯 Real-World Usage

  • Calculating total sales revenue or average product rating.

⚠️ Common Mistake

  • ❌ Trying to select non-aggregate columns without GROUP BY.

📝 Quick Task

  • Calculate COUNT(*) of registered users.

lessons.title: 15. Grouping Data (GROUP BY)
lessons.explanationHtml:
📌 What is it?

  • Groups rows sharing values into summary rows.

💡 Daily Life Example

  • Sorting coins into stacks of pennies, nickels, and dimes before counting.

🎯 Real-World Usage

  • Calculating sales per category, users per country.

⚠️ Common Mistake

  • ❌ Using WHERE instead of HAVING to filter grouped data.

📝 Quick Task

  • Group sales by country and SUM total revenue.
lessons.codeExample:

lessons.title: 16. HAVING Clause
lessons.explanationHtml:
📌 What is it?

  • Filters grouped rows after aggregation.

💡 Daily Life Example

  • Only keeping coin stacks that total more than $5.

🎯 Real-World Usage

  • Finding categories with average price > $100.

⚠️ Common Mistake

  • ❌ Using WHERE for aggregate functions (Use HAVING!).

📝 Quick Task

  • Group by category HAVING COUNT(*) > 10.
lessons.codeExample:

lessons.title: 17. Normalization Basics (1NF, 2NF, 3NF)
lessons.explanationHtml:
📌 What is it?

  • Organizing database structure to reduce redundant duplicate data.

💡 Daily Life Example

  • Filing receipts by store category instead of dumping all in one bag.

🎯 Real-World Usage

  • Building efficient, scalable database architectures.

⚠️ Common Mistake

  • ❌ Storing comma-separated lists of tags inside a single column.

📝 Quick Task

lessons.title: 18. Foreign Keys & Relationships
lessons.explanationHtml:
📌 What is it?

  • Links two tables together via a reference column.

💡 Daily Life Example

  • A library book receipt linking a student's ID number to a book's ID number.

🎯 Real-World Usage

  • Connecting Orders to Users, Comments to Posts.

⚠️ Common Mistake

  • ❌ Inserting foreign keys pointing to non-existent primary keys.

📝 Quick Task

  • Define user_id REFERENCES users(id) in Orders table.

lessons.title: 19. Inner Joins (INNER JOIN)
lessons.explanationHtml:
📌 What is it?

  • Combines rows from two tables where foreign keys match.

💡 Daily Life Example

  • Matching people's names with their reservation ticket numbers at a event gate.

🎯 Real-World Usage

  • Displaying Order details alongside Customer Name.

⚠️ Common Mistake

  • ❌ Missing ON clause condition in JOIN statement.

lessons.title: 20. Left Outer Join (LEFT JOIN)
lessons.explanationHtml:
📌 What is it?

  • Returns ALL rows from left table, even if no match in right table.

💡 Daily Life Example

  • A school attendance list showing all students, including those absent.

🎯 Real-World Usage

  • Finding users who have placed zero orders.

⚠️ Common Mistake

  • ❌ Confusing LEFT JOIN with INNER JOIN.

📝 Quick Task

  • Write a LEFT JOIN query finding users without orders.

lessons.title: 21. Subqueries
lessons.explanationHtml:
📌 What is it?

  • A query nested inside another query statement.

💡 Daily Life Example

  • Asking: 'Find all students whose score is higher than the average score'.

🎯 Real-World Usage

  • Complex analytical reporting.

⚠️ Common Mistake

lessons.explanationHtml:

  • Data structure that speeds up database query searches dramatically.

  • ⚠️ Adding indexes on every column slows down INSERT/UPDATE operations!

lessons.explanationHtml:

  • Financial transactions, inventory updates.

⚠️ Common Mistake

  • ❌ Forgetting to COMMIT or ROLLBACK open transactions.
